name: Archana Ghorpade
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Epilepsy, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease.
Patient reports occasional brief dizzy spells, mild exertional dyspnoea, and heartburn after meals. On exam: alert, oriented, BP 138/80, HR 78, SpO2 96% room air, lungs clear bilaterally, no wheeze or crackles, cardiac rhythm regular, no peripheral oedema, abdomen soft, no tenderness. She is on levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD, sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, spironolactone 25 mg OD, furosemide 40 mg OD, dapagliflozin 10 mg OD, pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, and antacid gel SOS. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Technique checked: correct for inhaler use (none prescribed). Smoking status: never smoked.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:

memories.author: D05
memories.text: EEG: background activity normal for age, no epileptiform discharges, no focal slowing. Impression: no acute epileptic abnormality; consistent with controlled epilepsy on current regimen.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling a bit of burning in my chest after spicy food, but it goes away with an antacid. My breathing feels fine when I walk around the shop.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025‑07‑10 at 10:00 am with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, stable epilepsy, mild GERD.
Patient notes increased swelling of ankles over past two weeks, occasional nocturnal cough, and heartburn after large meals. Exam: BP 142/84, HR 80, SpO2 96%, lungs clear, mild bilateral pitting oedema up to mid‑calf, JVP not elevated, abdomen soft. No new neurologic symptoms. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Technique checked: correct. Smoking status: never.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Furosemide increased to 60 mg once daily
All other medications unchanged.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum sodium 136 mmol/L (135‑145)
Serum potassium 4.8 mmol/L (3.5‑5.0)
Serum creatinine 82 µmol/L (45‑90)
NT‑proBNP 340 pg/mL (< 300) – mildly elevated

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram: Left ventricular ejection fraction 38 % (baseline 40 %). LV end‑diastolic diameter 5.6 cm. Mild mitral regurgitation, no significant aortic stenosis. NYHA class II. Impression: stable HFrEF, slight EF decline.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Refer to Cardiology for optimisation of heart failure therapy given rising NT‑proBNP and symptomatic fluid retention. Request echocardiogram review, consider uptitration of beta‑blocker and SGLT2 inhibitor if tolerated.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Cardiology review: Patient tolerated current regimen. Recommend increase bisoprolol to 5 mg OD if heart rate remains <70 bpm, continue dapagliflozin, monitor electrolytes. No urgent intervention needed. Follow‑up in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Stable epilepsy, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, worsened GERD.
Patient reports more frequent heartburn, especially after lying down, and occasional regurgitation. No new neurologic symptoms, dyspnoea on mild exertion improved after furosemide increase. Exam: BP 138/80, HR 72, SpO2 97%, lungs clear, trace bilateral ankle oedema, abdomen soft. No tremor. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Technique checked: correct. Smoking status: never.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Pantoprazole increased to 40 mg twice daily before breakfast and dinner
Domperidone continued 10 mg BD before meals
Antacid gel SOS unchanged

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Serum potassium 5.2 mmol/L (3.5‑5.0) – mild hyperkalaemia
Serum creatinine 85 µmol/L (45‑90)
NT‑proBNP 310 pg/mL (< 300) – slightly above

memories.author: patient
memories.text: The heartburn is bothering me at night; I have to sit up to sleep. My legs feel a bit swollen but not painful.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment changed: follow‑up moved from 2026-04-01 to 2026-02-28 at 09:30 am with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).
